summary: The injected TIMING DATA reported 0 commits since activation, but on-disk ground truth (ls results/ this turn + the already-committed ops/changelog.md and docs/research-log.md .423 entries) shows 12 artifacts (exp4579-exp4590) ran over a ~3h59m window (03:38->07:37 EDT). The locked structured fields are left at 0/0/0/null: experiments_completed=0 is the RECURRING milestone-scoped-detector false-zero (documented .363-.422, now .423), whereas compute_bound_experiments_count=0 and gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks=null are GENUINELY correct -- every .423 substrate was verifier_ensemble/aggregation/hardware_smoke and the frozen ARC sprint generator runs on the AMD iGPU, so both idle RTX 3090s are expected, not a bug.
bottlenecks_identified: Recurring timing-detector false-zero (the real operational bottleneck this milestone): the authoritative injected TIMING DATA block reported 0 commits since activation, yet 12 artifacts (exp4579-exp4590) are on disk for a ~3h59m window. This is an OBSERVABILITY failure documented across .363-.422 and now extending to .423 -- the shipped detector-wire repair reaches the standalone module but never reaches the conductor's retro prompt-assembly consumer that feeds this block.

NOT a GPU/compute bottleneck: compute_bound_experiments_count=0 is genuinely correct -- every .423 substrate was verifier_ensemble_against_cached_candidates / aggregation_from_upstream_artifacts / hardware_smoke, and the frozen sprint generator (Qwen3.5-9B-MTP) runs on the AMD iGPU per project policy, so the two RTX 3090s reading 0% util is expected (gpu_idle_on_compute_bound_tasks=null). No DualGPURunner concern: zero tasks loaded 2+ models on the monitored GPUs.

The false-zero forces every .423-class retro to fall back to manual on-disk ls/mtime + committed-changelog archaeology to recover the true experiment set -- slow, manual, and error-prone versus reading the injected block.
improvements_suggested: Root-cause fix (recurring .363->.423): MOVE the already-shipped detector-wire repair to the conductor's retro TIMING-DATA prompt-assembly call site. The standalone detector module is fixed, but the retro consumer that builds the TIMING DATA block does not call it -- which is why the false-zero keeps recurring.
Promote injected-commit-count == on-disk-artifact-count to a HARD retro-launch gate, so a false-zero is caught and corrected before the retro runs rather than reconciled afterward.
Stamp duration_s / inference_substrate / compute_bound on each artifact at WRITE time, so a retro can read per-experiment timing directly instead of reconstructing it from file mtimes.
No DualGPURunner enforcement is warranted this milestone (0 compute-bound tasks); keep both 3090s free for the next milestone that runs a monitored live_llm_inference task.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Wire the shipped detector repair into the conductor's retro TIMING-DATA prompt-assembly call site -- fixes the recurring false-zero (.363->.423) at its source so the retro reads the true 12-artifact set, not 0.
Gate retro launch on injected-commit-count == on-disk-artifact-count, so a miscount blocks (not silently passes) the retro.
Stamp duration_s/inference_substrate/compute_bound at artifact write time to make per-experiment timing directly readable in future retros.
meta_reflection: Execution was healthy -- 12 artifacts over ~3h59m, with a genuine headline positive (the live-submittable level count cleared the 33 score-lever baseline). The single recurring operational failure is observability, not execution: the retro's authoritative timing block false-zeroed AGAIN (.363->.423) because the detector-wire repair never reached the retro prompt-assembly consumer. compute_bound=0 and idle 3090s are genuinely correct here, so the only real action item is closing the detector false-zero at its source. estimated_time_savings_pct reflects retro/observability time (eliminating per-milestone manual on-disk reconciliation), NOT experiment wall-time, which was already fine.
